timeLimit: 1:00 per heat; three heats, best two count

competition.name: Competition #3: Concrete Conspiracy ’99 (Roswell, New Mexico)
competition.rules: Three heats per skater; best two heats count; runs judged on style, difficulty and variety; points deducted for falling; bronze, silver and gold medals

goals.text: Competition #3 Concrete Conspiracy ’99: three heats per skater, best two count, judged on style, difficulty and variety, points off for falling; bronze, silver, gold
Competition Park: a medal for a top-3 finish; the average of your top two runs is your final score

goals.text: At least bronze to beat the stage; collectibles: 2 stat points per style, Vicarious Visions logo, alien plushie

guidance: Night scene with floodlights on poles: the light-blue central deck is the brightest surface and draws the eye from the roll-in (LP1 0:27:39–0:27:43).
White chevrons on the kickers and halfpipe walls point the direction of travel (LP1 frames; VG).
“NO STEP” markings on the hatch and decks are a joke that also marks raised surfaces (VG).
The tunnel is lit green and the alien sits behind glass: a show-room that rewards entering the corridor (LP1 0:29:36–0:29:40).
Hidden on purpose: the pool room is behind doors in a halfpipe corner, out of the main sightline (G1 calls it a secret room).
Remake: neon-lit hangar look (LP12 0:36:55–0:38:25); stat points float over ramps near spawn.
designLogic: The final competition summarises vert: a roll-in channel, two halfpipes flanking a deck, a wrap-around halfpipe and a pool room. Street pockets (the deck rail, ET rails, B-House rails) hang off the vert structures rather than standing alone.

One central object scores many ways: over it (High Deck 1000, Low Deck 500), off its kickers (Deck Gap 1500), along its rail (Deck Grind 800), out of its top quarterpipe onto a far rail (MB Emerson 2000), and in the remake across its top (Cover Up 1000) and onto its hook rail (Nasty in the Pasty 1000).
Tony’s favourite spot is the High Deck Gap: the level’s signature move is clearing its central landmark.
The hidden room pays the most: the pool room holds a 2000-point gap, as much as the hardest open-hall gap.
A narrative room controls speed. The alien operation room sits in the corridor before the ET rails, and G1 tells you to slow down because the set-up after the doors is “extremely quick”.
Rhythm rails with variation recur twice: three rails out of the tunnel (the last curving right) and three rails at staggered heights on the back deck.
The longest transfer ends on a rail (MB Emerson). Precision comes at the end of maximum distance, not at the start.
The start gives speed: the roll-in feeds the ramp opposite, and G1’s line spends that speed on 720 grabs at once to fill the special meter.
Lighting is guidance in a dark level: floodlit deck, green tunnel, dark corners for the secret room.
The remake keeps the alien theme as gap anchors (Grey Grind, “Roswell That End’s Well”, a UFO in the pool room) and puts the plushie in the original’s secret room.
The remake puts the logo on top of the central deck: the most-used structure is crowned with the collectible.
Failure is cheap in each heat (falls land in halfpipes or on the flat), but the stakes rise across the career: this medal completes the set needed for the ending (G1 p135).
TAS1 clears the competition with two very short heats (5:32–5:50): judging scores the run’s best tricks, so the level needs a few dense combo spots near spawn.
remakeChanges: ET Grind is renamed Grey Grind (same three-rail description).
MB Emerson Grind is not in PS12’s gap list.
New gaps: Nasty in the Pasty (hook-shaped rail), Cover Up (manual on the deck-top quarterpipe), Roswell That End’s Well (manual past the alien).
The pool room gains a UFO and the alien plushie; stat points and a VV logo are added (PS12).
Look: the remake renders a neon-lit hangar; LP12 shows the “Overtime!” finish (0:37:50).
transfer: Hidden pool room: put the crystal on the far coping of a pool inside a side room, behind doors at a halfpipe corner. It is taken during a full-lap coping grind that needs one ollie over the entrance channel (the 2.1 m grind snap helps re-catch the coping).

Corridor before a rail chain: a short themed room (show-piece behind glass) forces a slow, straight approach. Right outside its doors, three rails in a row, the last curving. The crystal sits at the end of the third rail.

Crown the central deck: the crystal floats above a short quarterpipe built on top of the level’s central deck. Getting onto the deck is the first gate (press-up transfer from a side halfpipe), building speed on the small structure the second.

Rail at the end of the longest air: a crystal on a rail beyond a ramp lip, reachable only by a long transfer from the deck-top quarterpipe. Tune the distance to a pumped vert air, and make the landing a grind rail, not a ramp.
openQuestions: Where exactly are the ET/Grey Grind rails? VG labels “ET GRIND” at the NW corner ledge, G1 puts the rails just outside the tunnel’s second doors, and LP1’s tunnel exit (0:29:44) comes out at a chevron kicker.
Is MB Emerson Grind gone from the remake, or only missing from PS12’s list?
Heights of the decks and the deck-top quarterpipe are not measured.
Is the area outside the fence (helipads) skateable in either version?
TAS1 heats end after one short combo; whether this is by ending the run from the pause menu is not visible.
